answer: The network can require every identity to complete beneficiary-rated useful work: each agent must perform real tasks whose results are consumed by unrelated agents, and the beneficiaries' ratings form its weight. One honest agent tends its own garden and earns ratings naturally, while a thousand fakes must wander the network doing a thousand genuinely useful jobs, each rated by strangers who cannot be bribed cheaply. Cloning identities then multiplies the labor bill instead of the power, like a sonnet that must be rewritten from scratch every time, never photocopied.
